title: Per-tenant priority hedging and progressive evacuation for heterogeneous variant rollouts
creator: Daniel Kim
description: Background: We need a routing/fallback mechanism that supports tenant-scoped priority during variant rollouts. Some tenants are latency-sensitive (tier-1), others are cost-sensitive (tier-3). Current rollout tooling only supports uniform percentage-based canaries and global spillback when capacity is exhausted, which can cause low-priority tenants to evict high-priority traffic during regional congestion. Goal: implement a per-tenant hedging and progressive evacuation system that preserves KV/prefix caches where possible, enables soft-eviction lanes (non-disruptive spillback), and supports automatic rollback triggers based on quantile SLAs and error signatures.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Router supports tenant-priority weight buckets and will never evict higher-priority tenant traffic in favor of lower-priority tenants when capacity is constrained. 2) Progressively evacuating model variants moves traffic first from low-priority tenants to fallback variants/regions before touching high-priority tenants. 3) KV/prefix caches are preserved for sessions where traffic is routed to compatible fallback variants in the same KV domain. 4) Automatic rollback triggers perform canary-level rollback within 60s of SLA breach detection or persistent regression signals. 5) Integration test harness reproduces capacity tier spillback with tenant-scoped assertions.
technical_design: - Routing table will include tenant_priority (1-5) and tenant_affinity score. - Admission controller enforces priority-aware admission: tokens are allocated by tenant_priority and degraded when tier thresholds are hit. - Evacuation strategy: when a node/region is overloaded, router computes an evacuation plan that: (a) selects low-priority tenant sessions for spillback to fallback model variants/regions, (b) prefers fallbacks with compatible KV cache domains to avoid cold-cache penalties, (c) annotates requests with 'evacuation_reason' for observability. - Hedging: for tier-1 tenants, send parallel hedged requests to primary and a warm fallback (lightweight reserve) when measured tail latency approaches SLA quantiles. - Rollback: evaluate regression signals from canary metrics (latency P95/P99, correctness checks from eval prompts, error-rate spikes) and trigger automated rollback policy runbook with staged rollback percentages. - Safety: implement circuit-breaker thresholds per-tenant and a global emergency drain mode that only triggers with confirmed degradations and requires two independent signals (latency and correctness).
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Experiment): Feature-flag router with tenant_priority metadata; run internal canaries using sandbox tenants. Phase 1 (Limited): Enable for 10 customers (mix of tiers) in a single region with synthetic traffic; validate eviction ordering and cache preservation. Phase 2 (Regional): Expand to multi-region staged rollout with progressive evacuation stress tests. Phase 3 (GA): Turn on for all new rollouts, default off for legacy customers until opt-in. Each phase gated by integration tests and SLO targets.
test_plan: - Unit tests for priority-aware admission controller. - Integration harness simulating overloaded node and verifying eviction order by tenant priority. - Chaos test: randomly kill nodes and assert evacuation preserves KV affinity when half the fallbacks are compatible. - Canary regression test: inject subtle correctness drift and ensure automatic rollback triggers within target window. - Performance benchmark: measure added tail latency for tier-1 hedged requests under peak load.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk 1: Overcomplicating routing logic could introduce instability. Mitigation: keep heuristic simple; fallback to existing uniform spillback if algorithm fails health checks. Risk 2: KV cache preservation assumptions may be wrong across variants. Mitigation: conservative compatibility matrix; tag incompatible fallbacks and avoid cache-preserving optimization. Risk 3: Priority-based admission could starve low-tier customers. Mitigation: rate-limited eviction quotas and low-tier compensation policies (e.g., throttled non-critical requests, cheaper quantized model variants).
open_decisions: Define exact tenant_priority scale (1-5) and mapping to eviction buckets
Tolerance window for hedged duplicate requests before doubling token costs
Signals and thresholds for automated rollback (exact P95/P99 values and correctness delta)

2026-03-04 - Aisha Patel: Spike complete. Verified we can compute evacuation plans in <15ms for 10k tenant table. Draft PR opened for priority metadata (link above). Observed 8% extra headroom when preserving cache affinity.
2026-03-06 - Priya Singh (PM): Reviewed design. Request to add telemetry for 'evacuation_reason' and link to cost accounting so finance can simulate unit economics of hedging.

2026-03-07 - Eng-Review: Design reviewed by runtime team. Feedback: limit hedging to P99 approaching SLA and only for tenants with paid hedging flag. Action: update rollout plan and feature flag gating.
2026-03-09 - QA: Integration tests added to CI. Found edge case where dual-hedged requests doubled per-request billing for one tenant; added mitigation to deduplicate downstream cost events.
